title: Nottingham voters approve 12-month moratorium on data center development

facts.scope: any data center development within town limits

summary: Nottingham voters approved a 12-month town-wide moratorium on data center development on Sept. 8, 2026, giving the town time to study zoning changes. A developer's proposal had been withdrawn earlier in 2026.
source_title: NHPR (via WSHU) — Nottingham voters overwhelmingly approve moratorium on data centers
verbatims: Nottingham residents voted overwhelmingly Tuesday in favor of a 12-month moratorium on any data center development within town limits.
The vote was 1,335 in favor, to 143 against.
notes: Event date computed from 'Tuesday' in an article published Wed. 2026-09-09 (Tuesday = 2026-09-08). Article is NHPR syndicated. Not the state moratorium record; a town-level action.

title: Hawaii County Bill 170 would define and exclude industrial-scale data centers from county permitted uses; advanced to planning commissions

facts.last_reported_action: Leeward Planning Commission review scheduled 2026-10-15 (Star-Advertiser, 2026-10-03); outcome not found

summary: Hawaii County Council's policy committee voted to forward Bill 170, which defines industrial-scale data centers and leaves them out of permitted uses under county zoning, to the planning commissions. Status after the Oct. 2026 planning commission review is unknown.
source_title: Big Island Video News — Hawaiʻi County Council Forwards Data Center Bill To Planning Commissions
verbatims: voted to forward Bill 170 to the Hawaiʻi County planning commissions
notes: Event (committee vote) is July 7, 2026, before the Aug 1 window; included because the in-window status was reported Oct 3 and no Hawaii County record exists. Vote tally 8-0 from Star-Advertiser summary (WebSearch synthesis, not verified on BIVN page). Verify on Hawaii County council legislation page before merging. Zoning-exclusion bill, not a moratorium.

title: Boston councilor files order to bar data centers in every zoning district

facts.instrument: City Council order to amend zoning code
facts.proposed_treatment: prohibited use in every zoning district and subdistrict; variance path with community process per article

summary: A Boston city councilor filed an order that would define data centers and make them a prohibited use in every zoning district, referring to Gov. Healey's executive order. The order was on the Sept. 16 council agenda and was to be assigned to committee.
source_title: Boston.com (Boston Globe) — Boston City Council to consider zoning changes that would bar data center construction
verbatims: Councilor Miniard Culpepper filed an order this week that would amend the city's zoning code to define data centers and designate them as a "prohibited use in every zoning district and subdistrict" within the city.
notes: Article dated Sept. 15; 'this week' filing date not exact, so event_date is the article date. Proposal only. Healey EO 658 already tracked as ma-eo658-2026. Lowell (March 2026 one-year moratorium) and Westfield (July 2026) are out of window; not recorded here.

title: Sanford extends emergency data center moratorium 180 days (expires 2027-01-31)

facts.trigger: 1,000-acre Sanford Woods Industrial and Technical Campus proposal near the Mousam River

summary: Sanford's City Council unanimously extended its emergency data center moratorium for 180 days on Aug. 4, 2026, so it now expires Jan. 31, 2027. It overrides the original 91-day emergency moratorium.
source_title: Portland Press Herald — Sanford extends data center moratorium for 180 days
verbatims: The Sanford City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to extend an emergency moratorium on data centers for 180 days.
With the extension, the moratorium will expire on Jan. 31.
notes: Event date computed from 'Tuesday night' in an article dated Aug. 5 (Tuesday = 2026-08-04); corroborated by WGME dated Tue, August 4, 2026. Press Herald text was matched by probe on its opening clause; the 'Jan. 31' sentence appears in the same page text. Original May 2026 91-day moratorium is a separate event and not separately recorded here.

title: Eastport council adopts six-month moratorium on data center development

facts.scope: approving permits, licenses or applications for industrial data centers or computing facilities
facts.context: proposed underwater data center in Passamaquoddy Bay; ordinance proposals to permanently ban on the ballot

summary: Eastport's City Council unanimously adopted a six-month moratorium on data center development on Aug. 12, 2026, while it reviews a proposed permanent ban. Residents had also petitioned to put two ordinances to block the facility to voters.
source_title: Maine Public — Eastport enacts pause on data center development
verbatims: Councilors unanimously adopted the moratorium at an Aug. 12 meeting.
The pause runs for 180 days unless it is extended or the city passes a permanent ordinance banning data centers.
notes: Event date is the Aug. 12 meeting stated in the article. Probe matched both clauses on the Maine Public page.

title: Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly adopts 2027 legislative priority requesting data center moratorium

facts.vote: 6-1 (per search summary; not verified on source)
facts.requested_action: moratorium on permitting, leasing or construction of new commercial data centers on state/municipal lands, until state and local standards exist
facts.note: A request to the state and federal governments, not a borough ordinance

summary: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly approved 2027 legislative priorities that include a requested moratorium on new commercial data centers pending standards. The resolution asks the state and federal governments to act rather than regulating directly.
source_title: KUAC — In legislative priorities, Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly doubles up on AI data center moratorium request
verbatims: The Assembly's 2027 state and federal legislative priorities include a requested moratorium on data centers.
The Assembly resolution asks for a moratorium on the permitting, leasing, or construction of new commercial data centers
notes: Not a moratorium on its own. Record as a policy request. Article says the Assembly approved priorities Thursday (Aug. 27, 2026). KUAC notes the resolution text reads 'state-owned and municipal lands' while the presiding officer says federal lands were intended. Vote tally not verified on source.
